grammarPoints.title: Explanatory んです
grammarPoints.meaning: Connect a fact to the situation being discussed: explain, give relevant background, or invite an explanation.
grammarPoints.formation: Short predicate + んです. Nonpast affirmative nouns and na-adjectives use な before んです. Ask with んですか.
notes: Put tense and negation on the predicate before んです; keep んです itself unchanged in these patterns.
Use a real conversational reason for the explanatory tone. どうしたんですか often receives a reply with a new subject marked が.
Written のです has the same basic function in a more formal style. Casual んだ / の questions are noted in the book but developed later.

examples.english: I lost my wallet, you see.
examples.japanese: 財布をなくしたんです。
examples.kana: さいふをなくしたんです。

examples.english: You see, I am a teacher.

schemas.context: Someone notices you searching anxiously. Explain what happened.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Use なくした before んです. The context makes this an explanation rather than an isolated announcement.

schemas.context: Explain why you cannot go out late tonight.
schemas.kana: あしたは{event}があるんです。
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The event explains the present decision. Use short ある, not あります, before んです.

schemas.context: Explain why you do not want to go out tonight.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: An i-adjective attaches directly to んです: no だ and no な.

schemas.context: Someone is surprised you can keep working tonight. Explain why.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Negation belongs inside the explanatory construction, before んです.

schemas.context: Someone is surprised that you can help today. Explain your situation.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: A nonpast affirmative na-adjective needs な before んです.

schemas.context: Explain why you spend so much time at school.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: A nonpast affirmative noun needs な before んです. Do not use だんです.

schemas.context: A classmate has mentioned losing this item. Ask for the explanation.
schemas.japanese: どうして{item}をなくしたんですか。
schemas.kana: どうして{item}をなくしたんですか。
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The question seeks clarification of an already-mentioned event. It is not a neutral yes/no fact question.

grammarPoints.title: Excess with すぎる
grammarPoints.meaning: Say that an action or quality exceeds an appropriate amount.
grammarPoints.formation: Verb masu-stem + すぎる; i-adjective without final い + すぎる; na-adjective base + すぎる. Conjugate すぎる as a ru-verb.
notes: The sense is excessive or unwelcome. Use とても for a neutral “very” instead.
Do not leave い or な before すぎる. A resulting form such as 食べすぎました is a verb.

examples.kana: きょうしつはくらすぎます。

schemas.context: You regret the amount you consumed.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Express excess, not merely a large welcome amount. Conjugate すぎる as a ru-verb.

schemas.context: The room does not meet your needs.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Drop the i-adjective’s final い. The property is unwelcome in this context.

schemas.context: The material is unsuitable for this learner’s level.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Attach すぎる to the na-adjective base without な. Both excessive simplicity and complexity are unsuitable here.

grammarPoints.title: Advice with ほうがいい
grammarPoints.meaning: Recommend an action or advise against it.
grammarPoints.formation: Affirmative past short verb + ほうがいいです; nonpast negative verb + ほうがいいです.
notes: The past-looking affirmative form gives present or future advice, not a claim that the action already happened.
For negative advice use ない, not なかった. Advice can sound direct, so use an appropriate relationship or an invitation to advise.

examples.japanese: パンを食べたほうがいいです。
examples.kana: ぱんをたべたほうがいいです。

schemas.context: A friend asks which refreshments to try. Recommend this choice.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The affirmative action must be past short before ほうがいい; the advice concerns what to do now.

schemas.context: This particular refreshment tastes bad. A friend asks your advice.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Use the nonpast negative ない form, not past negative. This is advice, not a formal prohibition.

grammarPoints.title: Giving a reason with ので
grammarPoints.meaning: Join a reason to its result in a slightly more formal explanatory style.
grammarPoints.formation: Short reason clause + ので、result. Nonpast affirmative noun/na-adjective + なので.
notes: Keep the reason before the result. ので has a similar causal meaning to から.
Use なので after a noun or na-adjective in the nonpast affirmative; compare だから with から.

examples.english: Because I lost my ticket, I will not ride the train.
examples.japanese: 切符をなくしたので、電車に乗りません。
examples.kana: きっぷをなくしたので、でんしゃにのりません。

schemas.english: I will look for {item} because I lost it.
schemas.kana: {item}をなくしたので、さがします。
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The past event motivates the present action. Keep the past short verb before ので.

schemas.english: I will not go out because I am {state}.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The personal state plausibly prevents going out. I-adjectives do not take な before ので.

schemas.context: You attend school on weekdays.
schemas.english: I will go to school because it is {day}.
schemas.kana: {day}なので、がっこうにいきます。
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Use なので after a nonpast affirmative noun. The selected day must be a school day in context.

schemas.context: You are able to help today and explain why.
schemas.english: I will help because I am {state}.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Use なので after a nonpast affirmative na-adjective.

grammarPoints.title: Obligation: なければ / なきゃいけません
grammarPoints.meaning: Say that an action is necessary, including a past obligation or an informal “I have to.”
grammarPoints.formation: Take the nonpast negative ない form; replace final い with ければ or きゃ; add いけません. Past: いけませんでした. Casual: なきゃいけない or simply なきゃ.
notes: The overall meaning is affirmative obligation despite the negative-looking parts. It does not mean “must not.”
なければ is more formal; なきゃ is common in speech. Casual shortened なきゃ must suit the relationship.
Other variants exist, but these exercises focus on the two forms introduced here.

examples.english: I have to finish my homework.
examples.japanese: 宿題を終えなければいけません。
examples.kana: しゅくだいをおえなければいけません。

schemas.context: State an obligation in a formal or careful polite style.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The action is required, not prohibited. Build なければ from the negative form.

schemas.context: State your obligation in polite conversation using なきゃ.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Use the spoken contraction なきゃ but retain the polite final いけません.

schemas.context: Talk about last week’s obligation.
schemas.japanese: {day}に{task}を{action:obligationStem}ければいけませんでした。
schemas.kana: {day}に{task}を{action:obligationStem}ければいけませんでした。
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The final いけませんでした marks past obligation. Do not put the main action in past tense.

schemas.context: Tell a close friend casually. Use なきゃ.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Use a casual ending. The final いけない can be omitted without removing the obligation meaning.

grammarPoints.title: Tentative questions and guesses with でしょう
grammarPoints.meaning: Ask for an informed opinion gently, or make a tentative prediction.
grammarPoints.formation: Short predicate + でしょうか for a question; short predicate + でしょう for a guess. Remove nonpast affirmative だ after nouns and na-adjectives.
notes: Tense and polarity stay in the short predicate; でしょう remains unchanged.
たぶん can emphasize a guess. Casual rising でしょ can check agreement, but is different from the careful opinion question practiced here.

examples.english: Do you think it will be warm next week?
examples.japanese: 来週は暖かいでしょうか。
examples.kana: らいしゅうはあたたかいでしょうか。

schemas.context: Ask someone whose local weather knowledge may be better than yours. Use でしょうか.
schemas.english: Do you think it will be {weather} {time}?
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: This asks for an opinion, not an asserted forecast. Do not insert です or だ before でしょうか.

schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The adjective carries negation. This is a tentative language-practice prediction, not a factual weather report.

schemas.context: Ask for an informed guess about how busy or quiet it may be.
schemas.english: Do you think {place} will be {quality} tomorrow?
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: A nonpast affirmative na-adjective attaches directly to でしょうか without だ or な.

schemas.context: Ask a companion for a tentative opinion.
schemas.english: Do you think that person is {role}?
schemas.kana: あのひとは{role}でしょうか。
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: A nonpast affirmative noun attaches directly to でしょうか; omit だ.
